original_target.title: Real-rootedness of real powers of binomial coefficients

full_original_statement:
For every integer $`n\ge1`$ and real $`\gamma\ge2`$, does

```math
B_{n,\gamma}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk^{\gamma}x^k
```

have only real zeros? Repeated zeros are allowed. The constant and leading coefficients are one, so any real zeros are strictly negative. Powers act on the ordinary coefficients of $`(1+x)^n`$.

The target concerns these exact finite polynomials for every degree. It does not ask for a limiting zero distribution or for preservation on every real-rooted input polynomial.
queries: "binomial coefficients" "real powers" "real rooted" (site:arxiv.org OR site:zenodo.org OR site:hal.science OR site:github.com OR site:palomar-registry.org OR site:hexagonmath.org)
searched_channels: general web and primary author/publisher routing

sources.locator: §4.5 Remark4.8 lines473–475; EvidencePress specialist statement lines23–34
sources.scope_comparison: The final publication explicitly retains all n/all real gamma>=2 as a conjecture. Its limiting-measure formulas do not establish finite-degree real-rootedness. The actual EvidencePress candidate defines R4 with degree exactly4 and explicitly excludes arbitrary degrees. Even accepting that unrefereed announcement, it settles only a subcase.
